title: Human Computer Interaction: Main Exam, 17 April 2019
instructions: ANSWER ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A AND ANY OTHER TWO FROM SECTION B.

parts.text: Explain the following concepts as applied in HCI.

The user interface (UI) is a conduit between human and computer interaction: the space where a user will interact with a computer or machine to complete tasks. Discuss common characteristics of graphical user interfaces (GUI) as applied in computer technology.

In order to achieve effective HCI, fundamental principles have been established over the years by experts, among them flexibility. Examine the main elements of flexibility in enhancing system usability.
Prototyping is one approach in systems development that can be applied to achieve effective human computer interaction. Discuss essential requirements for prototyping tools.
As part of a user-centred focus, explain various techniques for customizing software to optimize human computer interaction.
As the field of HCI continues to grow, developers have innovated many techniques for enhancing system usability. Discuss the resource implications of a sophisticated HCI.
The user interface is one of the most critical components in HCI. As a systems expert, examine the effects of a poor user interface in computer-based information systems.
Learnability is one of the key principles in HCI and system usability. Discuss the factors that may affect the ease of learning software on the part of the user.
Examine the ergonomics aspects that are mainly associated with the use of computer-based information systems.
As a system developer, it is important to consider the needs of different types of users. Discuss the benefits and limitations that come with integrating sounds in a system interface.

A user interface can either be generic or specialized depending on targeted users and technical scope. Discuss the advantages and limitations of having a common user interface for different generic application programs in an organization.
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using a command-driven interface as compared to other types of interfaces that are common today.
